title: The base register preserves all 4695 provisional objects and 5680 faces
population: All 4,695 provisional Lipi families and 5,680 exported faces in register run-v2
finding: The base register preserves all 4,695 provisional objects and 5,680 exported faces, with 225,223 attributed assertions, 16,434 identifier rows and 11,993 measurement rows. All 4,695 objects retain unreviewed exposure status; zero are certified fresh.
scope: Families are provisional corpus identities. Source aliases do not merge them into adjudicated physical objects. The register preserves uncertain readings and excludes disputed cells from accepted fields. The [validation record](../../experiments/2026-10-22-object-register/VALIDATION.md) reports seven output files replaying byte for byte and 232,837 direct source-value comparisons with zero mismatches. The [coordinator's validation](../../experiments/2026-10-22-research-launch/VALIDATION.md) separately checks population and parent relationships. Those checks cover the stated source adapters and structural rules; physical identity and exposure review remain unfinished.

title: H-1657 has a published late Period 3C floor context
population: H-1657, identified as H99-4064/8796-1 in the 2010 Harappa manuscript and /8796-01 in HARP slide 56
finding: HARP slide 56 places H-1657 on the floor of Room 591 in Trench 43 and assigns it to late Period 3C. The 2010 manuscript's PDF page 3, footnote 4, supplies the catalogue-to-excavation identity link. This was the sole new object-context assertion in a five-case pass.
scope: The [separate source review](../../experiments/2026-10-24-harappa-context-pass2-review/REPORT.md) checked the original identity footnote and seven primary captions. Its reviewed scope is the identity and published floor attribution. The adjacent Period 4 vessel has a different key, H99/8763-503. The caption and manuscript belong to the same excavation lineage. Lot 8796's floor and wall sequence, phase argument and dated-sample link remain needed before this attribution can supply an independently established chronology label; no manufacture date was recovered.

title: H-1688 joins field key H90-1600 and lower Mound E street levels
population: H-1688 and the citation chain from Kenoyer and Meadow 2010 to Dales and Kenoyer 1991 Figure 13.44e
finding: H-1688 joins excavation key H90-1600/3166-1 and lower street levels in area C on the southern slope of Mound E, assigned to Period 3A. Dales and Kenoyer 1991, Figure 13.44e, printed p. 249 (PDF p. 65), supplies the key and context; the 2010 manuscript p. 10 identifies H-1688 and cites that figure.
scope: The [third-pass source review](../../experiments/2026-10-24-source-review-pass3/REPORT.md), Harappa row, checked this citation chain among twelve primary pages across four subjects. The field register and phase argument remain unchecked. The linked publications repeat one excavation lineage, and the pass added zero dated-sample links or manufacture dates. The result provides a named lot for further chronology work.

title: L-164 has conflicting published jar-stopper and wooden-box interpretations
population: L-164 = excavation 1864 = LTH SRG 1232, within the twelve-object L-161–172 elephant-sealing group
finding: Rao 1985, p. 319, describes overlapping cords on excavation object 1864's flat underside and interprets it as a flat-stoppered jar closure. CISI 1, p. 373, identifies that object as L-164. Frenez and Tosi 2005, pp. 78–79, include L-164 in their twelve-object group tentatively interpreted as wooden-box sealings.
scope: The [separate L-164 source review](../../experiments/2026-10-24-office-source-verification/REPORT.md) checked five primary page images and four source hashes. The common source observation is a cord-fastened flat underside. The later authors call box shape and size conjectural and leave packaging strings versus a fastening device unresolved. Registered, calibrated underside and edge views would decide the support geometry. The review establishes a disagreement between published reconstructions and leaves the physical specimen, die attribution and office conjecture outside its scope.

title: Rao assigns Plate CLXI F to two different Lothal objects
population: Plate CLXI F in Rao 1985 and the CISI 1 p. 373 identities of L-161 and L-164
finding: Rao 1985 assigns Plate CLXI F to excavation object 1864 on printed p. 319 and to 1830 on printed p. 325. CISI 1, p. 373, distinguishes them as L-164 = 1864 = LTH SRG 1232 and L-161 = 1830 = LTH SRG 1195. The inspected sources leave the photograph's object identity unresolved.
scope: The [third-pass source review](../../experiments/2026-10-24-source-review-pass3/REPORT.md), Lothal row, checked the contradictory references. The [object-pilot review v2](../../experiments/2026-10-26-object-pilot-review/REPORT-v2.md), section Register and unresolved identities, inspected fresh renders and the thematic index. Neither source selects the correct panel identity. The warehouse, layer and phase fields beside p. 325's entry cannot be transferred securely to L-164 through this panel. An original labelled negative register or specimen card would decide the binding.

title: Tell Brak REG257 is Matthews catalogue 308 and TB1058
population: Tell Brak REG257, catalogue 308 and TB1058 in Matthews 1997, with Eidem's Appendix B edition
finding: Matthews 1997, printed p. 265 (PDF p. 280), equates Tell Brak REG257, catalogue 308 and TB1058 and describes an irregular bulla fragment with crushed grooves on its back. Eidem's Appendix B, printed p. 308 (PDF p. 323), publishes a cup-bearer legend with part of the final name sign restored. The pass admitted zero legends to the comparison corpus.
scope: The [third-pass source review](../../experiments/2026-10-24-source-review-pass3/REPORT.md), Tell Brak row, checked the catalogue identity, carrier description and edition. Catalogue image number 257 is a different identifier from excavation registration REG257. This card records a source resolution; the originating acquisition attempt retains its exploratory status. Strict language classification, completeness and duplication against the frozen baseline remain open before this candidate can enter the readable-control population.

title: The H-2218 to H-2239 tablets share a reported cutting method
population: The complete 22-object incised steatite series H-2218–H-2239 in Meadow and Kenoyer 2000
finding: Meadow and Kenoyer report the same cutting direction and within-character stroke order across the 22 H-2218–H-2239 tablets, attributed to at least three engravers from microscopic examination of moulds. Sixteen tablets were recovered in a clump, two nearby and four scattered, all in secondary debris outside Mound E's curtain wall.
scope: The report's table gives PDF p. 16, author p. 15, mapped book p. 335, for the microscopic observation and engraver attribution; PDF p. 14 and the Figure 4 caption supply the recovery split. [Author validation](../../experiments/2026-10-24-tablet-use-evidence/validation-v1.json) checks the complete block and source accounting; no separate specialist review is recorded. The source leaves one workshop versus several and production timing unresolved. Its proposed pouch and ended utility are attributed interpretations. Physical-use evidence, including a registered ancient impression or attachment, remains needed.

title: The town register separates architectural axes and building episodes at 34 towns
population: The 34 candidate Harappan towns in Q-1032 register run-v5, including all eleven required towns
finding: The town register preserves 1,380 line and system records, 118 dated-part assertions and 620 radiocarbon assertions across 34 candidate towns. Wanzke's published Mohenjo-daro survey distinguishes nearly cardinal Moneer axes from the turned HR First Street axis, so one town-wide bearing would combine different architectural systems.
scope: The report's Primary-source checks section cites Wanzke printed pp. 33–44 and records 35 published rows with their original gon values and north distinctions. [Audit v5](../../experiments/2026-10-24-q1032-town-axis-register/audit-v5.json) checks 207 input hashes and 3,009 references; these are author record checks. Earlier independent orientation and plan-registration reviews are linked in the report, and their failed validation and error warnings remain attached to inherited values. Assertion counts include repeated uses of samples. No new radiocarbon determination or scientific orientation statistic is claimed. A surveyed wall requires its own construction-phase join before use in an orientation-date test.

title: Fourteen catalogue-view relations recovered from existing image assets
population: Twenty-four inspected assets and twenty source pages, compared with the 13 October image-files.csv assignments
finding: The image review supports fourteen new asset-to-catalogue view relations across thirteen existing assets and twelve catalogue keys. L-163 and L-207 gain their first keys in the 13 October image-file index. The L-163 A and C photographs were already held in source-page records, so the pilot gains zero newly available photographs.
scope: The [independent object-pilot review v2](../../experiments/2026-10-26-object-pilot-review/REPORT-v2.md), Image evidence section, checked all fourteen claimed relations against crop pixels, complete labelled plates and the prior index. It recreated twelve page renders and checked the 209 source and output bindings used in that review. The result is reviewed within that scope. The [corrected author report](../../experiments/2026-10-26-image-recovery/REPORT-v2.md) preserves the exact index baseline. This establishes index coverage without a new primary image file or physical-identity merge; thirty-four unresolved anonymous crops remain outside the selected block.
